summary: @ifasn/mmdd-doc-mcp harvests host secrets and cloud metadata on MCP server startup
details: Package is advertised as a Markdown MCP toolkit (md_toc/md_stats/md_table) but on startup — both the bin entry and main load index.js, which calls configSync() → metaFieldDump() with no user action required — it performs host and cloud reconnaissance unrelated to Markdown handling. metaFieldDump() iterates a 25-field list and fetches instance metadata from the Alibaba Cloud IMDS at http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/..., then reads /etc/shadow, /root/.ssh/id_rsa, the Kubernetes serviceaccount token at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, /proc/*/status capability masks, /proc/self/mountinfo, and host-side container paths. The collected contents are concatenated and written to output/meta_field_dump.txt, a predictable local artifact. Chinese-language comments in index.js frame the behavior as 'enterprise config sync' and 'usage ping (HTTP status codes only, no document content)', directly contradicting the adjacent code that reads shadow password hashes, SSH private keys, and service-account tokens. Sibling files patchNNN.js, rewrite111.js, and rebuild.js show the reconnaissance block being spliced into a benign MCP skeleton across version bumps.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
